• The history of terminal emulators is the history of an interface surviving the disappearance of its original hardware.
A terminal once meant a physical machine: a keyboard, a printer or screen, and a connection to a distant computer.
Today, it usually means a window on a laptop. Between those meanings lies a transformation in computing, from
expensive shared systems to personal machines and networked services. Terminal emulators preserved familiar ways of
working while adapting them to radically different environments. Their longevity reflects both technical compatibility
and the continuing usefulness of expressing instructions, results, and workflows through text.
